item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In June 2023, Germany’s state interior ministers committed to strengthen prevention of hate crimes and violence against LGBT people through law-enforcement training and police contact persons nationwide; the federal interior minister reported more than 1,400 hate crimes against LGBT people registered in Germany.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The measures and reported crimes concern 2023, while the report also provides 2022 baseline data.","ruler_attribution":"The measures were adopted by Germany’s interior ministers under the federal government led by Olaf Scholz; the source does not attribute each implementation outcome personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The source does not report implementation results or whether the measures reduced violence.","Reported figures may understate unreported incidents."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The coalition agreement promised to strengthen and expand Germany’s Anti-Discrimination Act, but by the report’s publication deadline the government had taken no action; the Federal Anti-Discrimination Agency had received 8,827 counseling requests in 2022, up 14 percent from 2021 and 50 percent from 2019.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.8","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The unfulfilled coalition commitment and agency status are reported for the 2023 period; complaint statistics are for 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The commitment belonged to Scholz’s coalition government, but the source does not identify Scholz as personally directing the delay.","limitations":["The source reports complaints and lack of legislative action, not adjudicated discrimination prevalence or later corrective action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In December 2023, the federal government adopted restructuring of the Federal Police Act that included mandatory records of police checks, a measure proposed in May to address racial profiling.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","4B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The proposal and adoption occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measure was adopted by Scholz’s federal government; the source does not show that Scholz personally designed or enforced it.","limitations":["The source does not provide evidence of enforcement, compliance, or effects on racial profiling."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Germany extended temporary protection for people fleeing Ukraine through 3 March 2024, allowing them to stay, work, and receive social protection; about 1.1 million Ukrainians were in Germany in April 2023.","question_ids":["2B.1","3B.7","6B.2","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The extension and population estimate concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The extension was enacted by Scholz’s federal government following the EU-level extension.","limitations":["The source also reports that asylum seekers and refugees spent weeks or months in crowded reception centers because of affordable-housing shortages."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Germany temporarily suspended a program intended to bring up to 1,000 vulnerable Afghans per month because of vetting concerns, later resumed it, but by the report deadline no Afghan had benefited from the program.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.6","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The suspension, resumption, and implementation failure are reported during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The decision was taken by the German government under Scholz; the source does not establish his personal role in the operational failure.","limitations":["The source does not quantify the number of people harmed by the delay."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"In August 2023, the government agreed on a draft Self-Determination Act allowing transgender, intersex, and nonbinary people to change their legal name and gender through a simplified administrative procedure without discriminatory expert assessments.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.8","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The agreement occurred in 2023; the source describes a draft rather than completed implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The draft was agreed by Scholz’s coalition government.","limitations":["The source does not establish enactment, funding, or practical access during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The European Commission found that Germany’s justice system lacked adequate resources and recommended stronger monitoring of lobbying in legislation and a legal basis for journalists’ access to information from federal authorities; Germany’s press-freedom ranking fell from 16th to 21st in 2023 amid violence and verbal attacks against journalists, declining media pluralism, fragmented information access, and proposed laws threatening source protection.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","5B.7","7B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The findings and ranking concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern German institutions during Scholz’s chancellorship but do not attribute the deficiencies personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The source combines Commission findings with a press-freedom ranking and does not isolate federal action from state-level causes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, Berlin authorities imposed a general ban on pro-Palestinian protests after escalating Israel-Palestine hostilities and rising civilian casualties; Human Rights Watch said they failed to assess necessity and proportionality case by case.","question_ids":["3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The ban occurred in October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The action was taken by Berlin authorities, not directly by Scholz’s federal government.","limitations":["The source describes a subnational decision and does not establish federal direction or later remedy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Germany’s Supply Chain Act entered into force in January 2023, requiring covered companies to identify, prevent, address, and publicly report human-rights risks in supply chains; the law limited administrative action and penalties to specified situations, excluded general court liability, and had limited reach across value chains.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.7","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The law entered into force in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The law was enacted under Scholz’s federal government; the source does not attribute its design personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The source does not report enforcement results or corporate compliance during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Police recorded 240,547 domestic-violence cases in 2022, an 8.5 percent increase over 2021; more than 70 percent of victims were women, and the government promised additional support including investment in shelters, while the shelter association said 14,000 additional places were needed.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The statistics are for 2022; government commitments and reported capacity needs are discussed in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The promised support was attributed to German authorities under Scholz’s government; the violence statistics predate the target year.","limitations":["The source does not show whether promised investments were executed or reduced violence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Germany ratified the ILO Violence and Harassment Convention in June 2023, establishing international standards for preventing and combating workplace violence and harassment.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Ratification occurred in June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Ratification was undertaken by the German government under Scholz; the source does not describe implementation measures.","limitations":["The source does not provide evidence of domestic enforcement or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"In January 2023, Bürgergeld replaced the previous basic-income-support system with slightly higher benefits; anti-poverty groups said the amount remained inadequate and criticized sanctions, while proposed child-poverty and rent-control measures had not been adopted by the report deadline.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The replacement took effect in January 2023; the report describes the status of further proposals during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Bürgergeld was introduced by Scholz’s coalition government.","limitations":["The source reports advocacy-group assessments rather than an independent incidence evaluation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":10,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Germany’s greenhouse-gas emissions fell 1.9 percent in 2022, but the Environment Agency expressed concern about increasing coal use; Climate Action Tracker said the government needed to do more to meet Paris Agreement commitments, while the government planned a heat-action plan.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The emissions result is for 2022; the assessment and planned heat-action response are reported in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The climate policies and planned heat-action plan concern Scholz’s government, but the reported emissions result predates 2023.","limitations":["The source does not report whether the heat-action plan was enacted or whether 2023 emissions improved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Germany published its first China Strategy in July 2023, describing Chinese human-rights violations and giving human rights conceptual priority, but it did not characterize abuses in Xinjiang as crimes against humanity and remained vague on implementation. During Scholz’s April meeting with China’s premier, journalists were not allowed to ask questions at the press conference.","question_ids":["2B.3","2B.6","4B.6","7B.1","7B.8","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The strategy and press-conference restriction occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The China Strategy was adopted by Scholz’s government; the source specifically places Scholz at the April meeting but does not say he ordered the press restriction.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the strategy produced subsequent policy changes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Germany continued coordinating international condemnation of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, provided extensive aid to Ukraine, and supported war-crimes investigations by the International Criminal Court and Ukrainian authorities.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.4","2B.9","2B.10","8B.3","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The activities are reported for 2023, against the background of the continuing invasion.","ruler_attribution":"These were policies of Scholz’s federal government; the source does not isolate Scholz’s personal decisions from coalition and international action.","limitations":["The source does not quantify the aid or assess its causal effects on the war or accountability."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e9e02551b0fefb48","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Germany supported Israel militarily after Hamas attacks in October 2023 but did not publicly condemn reported Israeli violations of humanitarian law in Gaza or emphasize accountability for all alleged international crimes; Human Rights Watch said this created a risk of German responsibility for war crimes.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.9","7B.1","7B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The conduct concerns the 2023 Israel-Hamas conflict.","ruler_attribution":"The policy was adopted by Scholz’s federal government; the source does not specify Scholz’s personal role in military-support decisions.","limitations":["The responsibility assessment is Human Rights Watch’s warning, not a judicial finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6a38f7a25ff8a411","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"On 28 November 2023, Scholz defended his government’s 2021 supplementary budget after the Federal Constitutional Court declared it unconstitutional and void for violating the constitutional debt rule and budget provisions; the government postponed the 2024 budget’s final consideration to assess the ruling.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","7B.2","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The court ruling and Scholz’s parliamentary response occurred in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the defense and response to Chancellor Olaf Scholz.","limitations":["The source reports the legal finding and political response but does not establish personal intent or culpability for the budget’s legal defect."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6a38f7a25ff8a411","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"After the constitutional ruling, the government proposed a 2023 supplementary budget to legally secure financing for gas and electricity price relief and flood-recovery aid, requiring an exception to the constitutional debt rule.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The proposal was made in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The proposal was made by Scholz’s federal government.","limitations":["The source does not report final enactment or implementation outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a3da0aef45987eda","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"In December 2023, Scholz said the coalition’s budget compromise would cut 12 billion euros from the Climate and Transformation Fund, close a 17-billion-euro 2024 core-budget gap partly by abolishing climate-damaging subsidies, reduce some ministry spending and federal grants, and preserve social security and transformation priorities.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The compromise and announced allocations concern December 2023 and the 2024 budget.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz directly presented and defended the coalition compromise.","limitations":["The source reports planned allocations, not executed spending or achieved outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a3da0aef45987eda","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"Scholz said the 2024 budget would include eight billion euros for weapons deliveries to Ukraine and more than six billion euros for Ukrainian refugees in Germany, and that Germany might declare a constitutional emergency if other supporters reduced aid and Ukraine’s situation worsened.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.8","2B.10","5B.9","6B.6","8B.3","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The commitments were announced in December 2023 for 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The commitments and contingency statement were made by Scholz on behalf of his government.","limitations":["The source does not report subsequent execution or whether the emergency exception was invoked."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a3da0aef45987eda","start_unit":24,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"The Bundestag approved coalition resolutions supporting the EU Commission’s recommendation to open accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova and rejected opposition resolutions; the approved resolutions called for continued reform in both countries.","question_ids":["2B.7","2B.10","4B.1","4B.4","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The parliamentary decisions occurred in December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The resolutions were supported by Scholz’s coalition and government position; the source does not attribute the parliamentary votes personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The fact concerns parliamentary approval of a position, not completed accession or durable settlement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7a16359b43126442","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Freedom House rated Germany Free with a 94/100 score in its 2023 report and described political rights and civil liberties as largely assured in law and practice within a stable representative democracy.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report is Freedom House’s 2023 country assessment, though parts of its evidence concern 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment covers Germany during Scholz’s chancellorship and the coalition government, not Scholz’s personal conduct alone.","limitations":["The score is an external aggregate assessment and does not isolate changes caused by Scholz in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7a16359b43126442","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Freedom House assessed Germany’s corruption safeguards as generally strong and effective but noted opaque party financing and insufficient lobbying regulation; it also reported that Scholz was questioned by a Hamburg parliamentary committee about alleged Cum-Ex-related tax avoidance and denied wrongdoing.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.5","7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report’s institutional assessment concerns 2022-2023; the questioning described occurred in August 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly identifies Scholz as having appeared and denied wrongdoing, but does not find that he committed misconduct.","limitations":["The allegations are not a finding of wrongdoing; the report predates the target year’s end for some events."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ac2407bd3f2a3781","start_unit":33,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"In November 2023, BMAS presented a commissioned research report on reforming earnings disregards and transfer-withdrawal rates to improve work incentives; the study used two representative surveys, optimal-tax analyses, ifo and ZEW microsimulation models, and an expert group, and developed concrete reform proposals including for the planned child basic income.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.9","6B.2","8B.1","8B.2","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The final report was submitted at the end of November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"BMAS commissioned the research under Scholz’s government; the source does not show that Scholz personally directed the study or implemented its proposals.","limitations":["The source describes analysis and proposals, not enacted reform or observed outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f4f1ae1656144534","start_unit":33,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"The BTHG financial investigation examined the financial effects of Germany’s disability-participation law on Länder and municipalities across six areas, using documentation, provider surveys, and statistical analyses; the main study from 2018-2022 continued in 2023-2024 to assess implementation, efficiency gains, and external influences on expenditure.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","6B.9","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The continuation of implementation research occurred in 2023, while much of the underlying study covers 2018-2022.","ruler_attribution":"The investigation was conducted for BMAS under Scholz’s government; the source does not attribute the research design personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The supplied text does not report the investigation’s substantive financial findings or service outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f663042f1eac4fba","start_unit":33,"end_unit":34,"fact_summary":"BMAS reported provisional 2023 social spending of approximately 1.249 trillion euros, up 5.2 percent from 2022; because nominal economic growth was 6.3 percent, the social-benefit ratio fell to 30.3 percent, below crisis-elevated levels in prior years.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The figures are provisional results for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The spending aggregate covers Germany’s social-security system during Scholz’s government; the source does not attribute the full total to Scholz’s discretionary choices.","limitations":["The aggregate does not show distribution, access, service quality, or causal effects attributable to the federal government."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2ab0763f2889a50b","start_unit":33,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"BMAS commissioned the ASID 2023 study, based on a representative register sample and a net dataset of more than 30,000 people, to analyze the living conditions and the type, amount, distribution, and determinants of income among people aged 60 and older, with differentiated analysis by sex and region.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.8","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The study is identified as ASID 2023; the supplied text describes its research design rather than findings.","ruler_attribution":"BMAS commissioned the study under Scholz’s government; no personal Scholz role is stated.","limitations":["The supplied units do not provide substantive pension-income findings or policy outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-91cf3cbfa69d286b","start_unit":33,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"BMAS reported that Germany implements the UN Sustainable Development Goals through a periodically updated German Sustainable Development Strategy, prioritizing poverty reduction, decent work and growth, and reduced inequality; it also stated that BMAS was establishing an EU EMAS environmental-management system and using employment, training, and continuing-education measures to support these goals.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","6B.1","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report concerns 2023 administrative priorities and ongoing implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The described priorities and EMAS establishment concern BMAS under Scholz’s government, not necessarily personal decisions by Scholz.","limitations":["The supplied text gives no quantitative outcome indicators and does not establish completion of the EMAS system."]},{"source_id":"SRC-192f16f6da169df0","start_unit":33,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"The disability-participation survey used a representative sample of 22,000 people aged 16 and older, including people in private households, supported living arrangements, and senior facilities; conducted from 2017 to 2021, it applied the ICF framework to identify participation barriers and included groups often missed by surveys.","question_ids":["6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The study was conducted in 2017-2021 and reported as a research basis available during the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The study was commissioned by BMAS under Scholz’s government, but its fieldwork predates his chancellorship.","limitations":["The supplied text states the method and purpose but gives no concrete 2023 outcome or policy implementation result."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-378a977c385baddb","SRC-4c03fc62f1b425d2"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied BMAS pages consist largely of navigation boilerplate; only their substantive publication blocks were treated as evidence.","The supplied documents provide limited direct evidence about Scholz personally; many facts concern the federal government, BMAS, Parliament, or subnational authorities during his chancellorship.","No source supplied concrete evidence relevant to nuclear-risk questions 1B.1-1B.10."]}
